Apex Peptides

US gray market· Injectables & peptide blends· Scored July 2026· apex-peptides.com →
44 /100
Limited Transparency
Testing appears to happen and community reports suggest real COAs exist - but every documentation input is locked behind account creation. A stranger cannot verify any of it from public materials before purchase.
Dimension Scores
DimensionScoring NotesScore
Third-Party Testing Practice
Community feedback (PeptideCritic, April 2026) describes COAs as "REAL" and "complete," and the vendor support widget references COA access. However, the testing lab name, method (HPLC / MS), frequency, and catalog coverage are not stated anywhere publicly accessible - all are presented only after account login. Cannot confirm per-batch third-party testing from public materials alone. Partial credit for community corroboration of practice, not for publicly documented practice.
 16 / 30
Batch Traceability & Verification
Community references confirm batch numbers appear on vials. However, the corresponding COA match requires account login to access. No public-facing lot verification tool, scannable code resolving to lab records, or open archive. A stranger cannot verify their vial against any public record before or after purchase without creating an account.
 8 / 20
COA Accessibility
Every public-facing page - homepage, product pages, FAQ, and shop - returns a login wall. The support widget explicitly lists COAs as a post-login feature alongside orders and discounts. This is more restrictive than email-request gating: account creation is required before any documentation is reachable. Minimum-tier score; one step above fully absent.
 4 / 15
COA Completeness
No publicly available COA to assess directly. Community description of COAs as "complete" and "REAL" suggests meaningful documentation exists post-login. Partial credit for corroborated completeness. Without a publicly viewable COA showing test type, issuing lab, chromatogram, and lot linkage, completeness cannot be confirmed from the outside.
 8 / 15
Testing Recency
No COA dates are publicly visible. Recency of testing relative to currently sold product cannot be assessed without login. Minimum score for inability to verify.
 4 / 10
Policy Transparency
FAQ and policy pages are login-gated. One policy term - "All sales are final" - is discoverable in a search cache snippet as of July 2026. Reship terms, refund scope, and conditions are not publicly stated. Near-minimum score; one visible term is marginally above none.
 1 / 5
Operational Track Record
Trademark "APEX PEPTIDES" filed March 11, 2025 by Apex Performance Longevity Group LLC (USPTO serial 99077782), confirming an LLC entity and registered mark. Community reviews reference 1+ year of customer relationships as of April 2026. Veteran-owned operation. Established but under two years at time of scoring.

Community Signal
Independent Test Results
No community-commissioned independent test results (third-party purchase and lab submission) identified in public forums as of July 2026. This field will be updated as independent results are published.
Community Experience
PeptideCritic community (April 2026) includes a reviewer with 1+ year of purchase history describing products as "real and high quality" and COAs as "REAL" - explicitly noting authenticity as a differentiator. Military discount program (55% off) and veteran ownership referenced positively. Pricing flagged as high at full price. Separate community discussion noted that some products use branded blend names ("Vitality Vibe," "Tri Immune Blend") rather than compound names in the public shop, making pre-login identification difficult. General community signal: positive on product consistency and COA authenticity; mixed on value and site navigation.
Scoring Notes
The login gate is the ceiling
The score is not primarily about whether testing happens - community signal suggests it does. The score reflects that a stranger cannot verify any of it. When every documentation input sits behind account creation, the seven-dimension rubric has almost nothing public to assess. Test method, issuing lab, lot linkage, COA dates, and policy terms are all unreachable before purchase. That is the structural problem the Limited band captures.
What a score revision would require
Making COAs publicly accessible - even behind an email-request gate rather than account creation - would move the COA Accessibility score from 4 to 9 and unlock meaningful points in Traceability and Recency as well. A publicly visible policy page would close the Policy gap. Combined, those changes would push the score into the Moderate band without any change to underlying testing practice.
